trust_decision.summary: Whether a DID field names the caller is decided only at tx level by the IID ante (the signer account must hold an authentication/assertion relationship on the GetIidController DID) and is never re-checked inside the module keepers; separately, x/bonds resolves a caller-supplied verification-method fragment to a bech32 address and spends from it without ever comparing that address to the message's own *_address signer field, so on ICA/wasm/authz routes nothing decides it at all.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary leads with 'x/bonds DID-resolved payer drain'; the first code an engineer opens is Buy, which looks up BuyerDid's document, resolves the fragment to an address at line 437 and debits that address at line 469 without ever reading msg.BuyerAddress (the proto signer field, proto/ixo/bonds/v1beta1/tx.proto:182).

fix_sites.entry_point: x/bonds Msg service: CreateBond, EditBond, SetNextAlpha, UpdateBondState, Buy, Sell, Swap, MakeOutcomePayment, WithdrawShare, WithdrawReserve

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The ICA host AllowMessages allow-list is an app upgrade/config parameter, not module authorization code; the report and the failing tests are about handler checks, so a solver leaves '*' in place and treats app/upgrades as out of scope.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Delegated claim submission/evaluation: MsgSubmitClaim, MsgEvaluateClaim and MsgCreateClaimAuthorization carry the collection admin in their proto signer (admin_address) while their *_did field names a DIFFERENT party (agent/creator) as attribution only; they are legitimately authorised by authz grants and collection.Admin, so a blanket 'every IidTxMsg must prove signer controls its DID in the keeper' fix wrongly requires the admin to control the agent's DID and breaks delegated claims.

O6_input_shapes: DID string carrying a fragment (e.g. did:ixo:x#key-2) vs the bare DID vs the document Id method
message at top level vs the same message nested inside authz.MsgExec (recursively, and beyond a depth bound)
single-element token batch vs multi-element batch of one contract vs mixed-contract batch
batch element with empty id vs zero amount vs amount greater than current supply
ICA host with allow-all '*' vs an explicit type-URL allow-list (and ixo/authz/wasm type URLs inside it)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: First-swapper buy branch: Buy returns early into performFirstSwapperFunctionBuy, which re-resolves BuyerDid and deposits from the resolved address before the normal SendCoins sink
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is a subroutine of Buy in the same file, so a check placed at the line-469 sink looks like it covers the handler.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, 35 lines below the landing point (resolution at x/bonds/keeper/msg_server.go:503-511, debit at :530)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: EndBlocker batch settlement: PerformBuyAtPrice / PerformSellAtPrice / PerformSwap resolve BaseOrder.AccountDid to an address and mint, pay out or refund to it
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Orders only enter the batch through the msg handlers, so a handler-side signer check is assumed to cover settlement; the published fix closed it by no-op'ing EndBlock (fix.diff:852-856), not by checking the batch resolution.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: second implementation in another file of the same package; six resolver sites (x/bonds/keeper/batch.go:216, 365, 433, 559, 639)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: MsgCreateEntity over a CosmWasm-stargate / ICA-host dispatch: the keeper never verifies that the signer controls OwnerDid before registering it as controller of the new entity DID
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Creation only mints new state (a fresh DID document plus an NFT); no existing entity or funds are mutated and OwnerDid is arguably just an initial controller declaration.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the three fixed handlers but a different message and an earlier function (x/entity/keeper/msg_server.go:35-152); the published fix adds VerifyDidSignerAuthentication to the other three entity IidTxMsg handlers only

O8_uncovered_routes.route: MsgExecuteContract against the entity NFT contract dispatched as a wasm sub-message (or via ICA host), which never passes the entity ante decorator
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The decorator only sees the transaction's own messages; the published fix's own comment states the route-proof fix is a contract-level restriction, so leaving sub-messages open reads as an accepted limitation.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package; the fix only adds authz.MsgExec recursion (fix.diff:1107-1117)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new DID-gated claims handler that calls AuthorizeAdjudicator with a caller-supplied adjudicator DID
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The module already has the exact authorise-as-a-DID pattern inside the keeper and new claim/dispute messages are added regularly; a fresh handler that forgets the signer-relationship argument looks natural.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new token handler that resolves a DID fragment to a payout address, mirroring the bonds payer pattern
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Token handlers already take a batch plus an owner address and execute against a cw1155 contract; a DID-owned variant is an obvious next feature.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A later upgrade that re-adds a type URL (or '*') to ICAHostKeeper AllowMessages
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This file already sets the allow-all default once; re-widening the list to 'support ICA users' is exactly the change that reopened the class.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second fragment-to-address helper (or a purpose-filtered variant) used by a new module without binding the result to the signer
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The resolver is a public type-level API that takes any verification-method id and never checks its relationship purpose, so copying it is the shortest route to a DID-driven payout.
